draft.title: Solubility
card: Solubility is the maximum mass of a solute that dissolves in a given amount of solvent at a set temperature, such as g per 100 g of water. A solution holding that maximum is saturated.
A solubility curve plots solubility against temperature. A point on the curve is a saturated solution. A point below it is unsaturated, and more solute can still dissolve.
For most solids, solubility rises as temperature rises, so the curve slopes up. If a saturated solution is cooled, the extra solute comes out as crystals.
For gases, solubility falls as temperature rises, so the curve slopes down. A warm drink holds less dissolved carbon dioxide than a cold one.
draft.remember: Solids usually dissolve better when hot. Gases dissolve better when cold.

a.q: A solubility curve shows a solid dissolving at 40 g per 100 g of water at 50 °C. A solution at 50 °C holds 25 g in 100 g of water. How is it best described?
opts: Unsaturated, as more solute can still dissolve
Saturated, as the solute has all dissolved
Saturated, as it is below the curve
Unsaturated, as it holds less than 100 g
a.why: The curve gives the maximum at 50 °C, which is 40 g. A solution with 25 g holds less than this, so more solute can dissolve and it is unsaturated. Having all the solute dissolved does not make a solution saturated.
a.clue: Compare 25 g with the maximum at that temperature.

b.q: Mia cools a saturated solution of a solid in water from 60 °C to 20 °C. The solid's solubility rises with temperature. What happens?
opts: Crystals form, as the solid is less soluble at 20 °C
Nothing, as the solution is still saturated and clear
Crystals form, as cold water cannot dissolve any solid
The solution becomes unsaturated as the solid dissolves
b.why: This solid is less soluble at 20 °C, so the water can hold less than before and the extra comes out as crystals. Cold water still dissolves some of the solid, so the idea that it dissolves none is wrong.
b.clue: Read the curve at the lower temperature.

a.best: Unsaturated, as more solute can still dissolve

b.best: Crystals form, as the solid is less soluble at 20 °C

problems.detail: The clue says 'Read the curve at the lower temperature', but question b gives no curve or values. Students are told only that solubility rises with temperature, so the clue points to information that isn't there and could confuse them.
